# Lookup tables for both classifications {#sec-lookup}

Before ingesting and validating expert cross-referencing records, we construct formal **lookup tables** (`lookup_tbl` objects from the `ecoSynthesis` package; @ecoSynthesis_pkg) for both the source classification (TASVEG 5.0) and the target classification (IUCN GET Level 3). These controlled vocabularies define the complete set of valid unit codes, their human-readable names, and—for the source classification—which units passed the conceptual alignment screening in @sec-alignment (`eligible = TRUE` vs `FALSE`).

## Source classification: TASVEG 5.0

For TASVEG 5.0 [@TASVEG_5], we build the lookup table from the official Fire Attributes `.dbf` table distributed with the statewide release. Using the lightweight `.dbf` file avoids loading the full polygon geometries during the data preparation stage.

:::{.aside}

Our setup for this R session loads the DBF reader (`foreign`), data manipulation tools (`dplyr`, `readr`), and `ecoSynthesis`, and points `output_dir` to `results/XREFs`:

```{r}
#| warning: false
#| message: false
here::i_am("preparation/lookup-tables.qmd")
library(foreign)
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(ecoSynthesis)
output_dir <- here::here("..", "results", "XREFs")
```

Make sure the TASVEG 5.0 archive has been downloaded into `gisdata/` first (see @sec-source):

```{r}
#| filename: "scripts/TASVEG-data-download.R"
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Download source data / TASVEG 5.0"
#| file: ../../scripts/TASVEG-data-download.R
```

:::

First, we read `TASVEG_5_0_Fire_Attributes_LUT.dbf` with `as.is = TRUE` so character codes and descriptions are kept as strings rather than factors:

```{r}
TASVEG_DBF <-
    read.dbf(
        here::here("..", "gisdata", "LIST_TASVEG_50_STATEWIDE", "TASVEG_5_0_Fire_Attributes_LUT.dbf"),
        as.is = TRUE
    )
```

From this attribute table we retain the three fields that identify each vegetation community and its higher-level TASVEG group:

| Attribute Name | Full Name | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `VEG_GROUP` | Vegetation Group | Broad vegetation group to which the community belongs; useful for hierarchical summaries and display. |
| `VEGCODE` | Vegcode | Three-letter code that uniquely defines the TASVEG mapping unit (`source_id`). |
| `VEGCODE_D` | Vegcode Description | Full name of the vegetation community described by `VEGCODE`. |

Next, we select these three columns, sort them alphabetically by vegetation group and code, remove duplicate rows, and convert the result to a tibble (`TASVEG_LUT`):

```{r}
TASVEG_LUT <-
    TASVEG_DBF |>
    select(VEG_GROUP, VEGCODE, VEGCODE_D) |>
    arrange(VEG_GROUP, VEGCODE) |>
    unique() |>
    as_tibble()
```

The interactive table below allows browsing and searching all `r nrow(TASVEG_LUT)` `VEGCODE` entries defined in the TASVEG 5.0 Fire Attributes table:

```{r}
DT::datatable(TASVEG_LUT)
```

Following the conceptual alignment assessment in @sec-alignment, we flag the three non-eligible mapping units (`OAQ`, `OSM`, and `ORO`) using the negative-matching operator `%nin%` from `ecoSynthesis`, and wrap the table into an `ecoSynthesis::lookup_tbl` object that stores column metadata (`id`, `name`, and `eligible`):

```{r}
not_eligible <- c("OAQ", "OSM", "ORO")
TASVEG <- TASVEG_LUT |>
    mutate(eligible = VEGCODE %nin% not_eligible) |>
    lookup_tbl(id = "VEGCODE", name = "VEGCODE_D", eligible = "eligible")

TASVEG
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Local DBF lookup table vs. bundled `ecoSynthesis::TASVEG_LUT`
The `ecoSynthesis` package also bundles a convenience dataset `ecoSynthesis::TASVEG_LUT` containing the **156 mapped units** extracted from `TASVEG_5_0.shp`. In this workflow we build `TASVEG` directly from `TASVEG_5_0_Fire_Attributes_LUT.dbf` (**159 entries**, including three codes—`FPL`, `HUE`, and `SLW`—that are defined in the manual but absent from the statewide polygon shapefile) so the lookup table reflects the complete authoritative classification vocabulary.
:::

## Target classification: IUCN GET

The [IUCN GET controlled vocabulary](https://w3id.org/iucn-get/IUCNEcosystemTypology) [@Keith_2022] defines all units in the upper three levels of the typology (Realms, Functional Biomes, and Ecosystem Functional Groups).

Here we wrap the `IUCN_GET_LUT` dataset bundled in `ecoSynthesis` into a `lookup_tbl` object. Because `eligible` is omitted (`NULL`), `lookup_tbl()` automatically marks every IUCN GET Level 3 Ecosystem Functional Group as eligible (`eligible = TRUE`):

```{r}
IUCN_GET <- lookup_tbl(IUCN_GET_LUT, id = "efg_id", name = "efg_name")
IUCN_GET
```

:::{.aside}

We save both `lookup_tbl` objects (`TASVEG` and `IUCN_GET`) to `results/XREFs/lookup-tables.rda` so subsequent preparation, validation, and synthesis chapters can reload them without re-reading the source DBF:

```{r}
save(TASVEG, IUCN_GET, file = here::here(output_dir, "lookup-tables.rda"))
```

:::
